name: Bed Maker
label: Dischord
lede: Four DC lifers played one show in February 2020 before the pandemic shut it down. The debut LP came out on Dischord in 2024, and a 7" followed in 2026.

eras.title: Nobody was new
eras.text: The rhythm section had played together in Alarms & Controls, the guitarist made tape and field-recording music as Insect Factory, and the singer had been in DC punk since the late '80s. They got one show in before the world stopped.

years.h: Noll and Novara call Jeff Barsky to see what happens
years.p: Bassist Arthur Noll and drummer [[Vin Novara|bfec86c6-f1ae-4915-ac83-c1806a929118]], old [[Alarms & Controls|2db28ba7-b327-4926-aff2-0838913e6b39]] bandmates, ask guitarist Jeff Barsky of [[Insect Factory|ed9de18b-efae-478c-bd07-bc17214a36b7]] to come jam.
years.xp: Noll also played in [[Light Beams|42b3e741-bdf8-402e-acdf-f73c2a491951]] and Kid Congo Powers' band. Novara drummed in [[The Crownhate Ruin|6c13db70-bd59-44a0-8c6a-eeb0d0c8f40d]] and [[1.6 Band|e3b548df-c063-4603-bac1-1b01fcf84ef2]]. Barsky also played in [[Time Is Fire|636587a0-55da-492f-9e22-b3d9cf7c35f4]].

years.p: MacKaye had sung in Desiderata, [[Routineers|16e1e50b-c155-479b-8b74-432c899e1520]] and Jury Rig, and co-founded Sammich Records, home of [[Swiz|eea2f3d8-1e94-436c-ae66-4633f99f55be]], [[Soulside|de2e8176-32c2-4abe-b718-9392dffd8ffe]] and [[Shudder to Think|5a6e19e0-3ff0-4b3d-869e-3c539d6d8707]]. Her brother is [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]].

years.h: Rhizome hosts the first Bed Maker show
years.p: The debut is at Rhizome, the DC arts space, in February 2020.

years.h: One month later, the pandemic stops the band
years.p: Bed Maker stops playing in March 2020, as most bands did, Dischord notes.

eras.title: An act of defiance
eras.text: Two and a half years later they came back and went straight to work on a record, split between a Maryland home studio and the Inner Ear basement, where Dischord records have been made since the early '80s.

years.cap: Bed Maker at Comet Ping Pong, Washington DC, March 18, 2023
years.h: After two and a half years off, Bed Maker plays out again
years.p: Dischord dates the return to November 2022, with a record already on the way.

years.h: Full set filmed by hate5six, September 22, 2022

years.cap: Bed Maker at Comet Ping Pong, Washington DC, June 22, 2024
q: An act of defiance to the horrors of the last four-plus years.
years.h: The debut LP lands as Dischord No. 197
years.p: Ian MacKaye and [[Don Zientara|a495882b-4585-4295-9269-e30c63f279fe]] finished it at Inner Ear in 2023. Dischord released Bed Maker on May 31, 2024.
years.xp:
Earlier sessions ran with [[Mike Schleibaum|44059ab7-0b66-472a-87dc-db3557dcd1b7]] and Matt Michel at Viva Studios and at Schleibaum's home studio in Maryland. Ian MacKaye is singer Amanda MacKaye's brother, and Dischord's notes say the LP only exists thanks to family and many friends. Eleven songs, from Two Left Feet and Candy Striper's Confession to Miss Dickens and Pan-Pan; Ballad of Tokitae was the preview track.

Bandcamp Daily made it an Album of the Day. Reviewer Jennifer Kelly wrote that "The sound is noisy but disciplined", heard a line back to the [[Minutemen|d4ad0149-d8ae-4105-8009-0221fce9ff35]]'s stops and starts, and heard Amanda MacKaye singing about the everyday weight of women's oppression, with domestic labor as the image.

eras.title: Two songs, two days
eras.text: The follow-up was The Mark and What Boy Where, cut in two days, and the band took them on the road.

years.cap: Bed Maker at Smash Records, Washington DC, December 22, 2024
years.h: Two days at Tonal Park become the The Mark 7"
years.p: Bed Maker recorded The Mark and What Boy Where in October 2025. Dischord released the 7" as No. 203 on September 11, 2026.
years.xp:
Ian MacKaye and Don Godwin recorded and mixed the two songs on October 3 and 5, 2025 at Tonal Park. Dischord calls them tightly wound. Cover art is by Luna Novara, layout by [[Jason Farrell|f458f662-c72b-485b-9152-81eda8659fdb]].

It is the band's first new material since the 2024 debut.

yt: Two Left Feet, Ottobar, Baltimore, March 2026
years.h: Four nights on the road behind The Mark
years.p: Charlottesville on the 25th at the University of Virginia, Durham on the 26th at the Fuzzy Needle, Hyattsville on the 27th at Shady Lane Records, Harrisonburg on the 29th at Wizard Mode Brewcade.
